name: Eric Engstrom
milestone_by_age_26: Material fame arrived at about age 30 with DirectX (revealed ~April 1995, shipped with Windows 95 later that year); no specific material public milestone by age 26 found (returned to Microsoft as technical evangelist by 1991).
early_history_summary: Born 1965 in Oroville, Washington; attended but did not finish Washington State University; self-taught programming while working odd jobs; briefly at Microsoft in customer-support consulting, then Data I/O, returning to Microsoft by 1991 as a technical evangelist before co-creating DirectX with Alex St. John and Craig Eisler in 1994–95.
evidence_summary: Engstrom’s defining achievement—DirectX as a Windows gaming API—came at about age 30. Earlier Microsoft employment by age 26 is not a comparable material milestone. He later founded Wildseed (acquired by AOL), returned to Microsoft, and died in 2020 at 55.

name: Kerry Davis
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; DigiPen graduate (2006) and longtime Valve developer (credited ~15 years by 2019) but no dated material milestone verifiable at age ≤26.
early_history_summary: Kerry Davis graduated from DigiPen Institute of Technology in 2006 and became a long-tenured Valve engineer working on titles including Half-Life: Alyx VR interaction design; public profile centers on later Valve/VR work.
evidence_summary: Without a documented birth year, age at any Valve or DigiPen milestones cannot be verified. No independent Wikipedia biography establishes an early dated breakthrough by 26.

name: Andrei Broder
milestone_by_age_26: PhD under Knuth completed in 1985 at age ~32; major web contributions (shingling/min-hash, CAPTCHA, AltaVista, bow-tie web graph) came in his 30s–40s; no material dated milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born 1953 in Bucharest to physician parents; emigrated to Israel in 1973; B.Sc. summa cum laude from Technion (1977, age ~24); PhD Stanford under Donald Knuth (1985); later DEC SRC, AltaVista, IBM, Yahoo, Google.
evidence_summary: Technion graduation at ~24 is educational, not a field-defining breakthrough. Landmark algorithms and industry leadership (AltaVista CTO, computational advertising, Kanellakis Awards) occurred well after age 26.

name: Alfred Lutter
milestone_by_age_26: At age 12 starred as Tommy opposite Ellen Burstyn in Martin Scorsese’s Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore (1974), earning a BAFTA nomination for Most Promising Newcomer; followed with roles in Love and Death (1975) and The Bad News Bears (1976) before age 15.
early_history_summary: Born March 21, 1962 in Ridgewood, New Jersey, Lutter was cast after Scorsese’s team auditioned hundreds of boys; his improvisational chemistry with Burstyn made him a standout child performer through the mid-1970s. He later left acting, earned BS (1984) and MS (1988) degrees from Stanford, and founded Lutter Consulting in June 1986 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Ridgewood, New Jersey; parents later referenced in a wedding announcement as living in Rancho Bernardo, California. Detailed family financial or industry background not documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: child actor, Scorsese, BAFTA nominee, Bad News Bears, Stanford engineering, consulting founder
evidence_summary: Lutter’s material breakthrough was early film work: a major Scorsese feature at 12 with BAFTA newcomer nomination, then Woody Allen and Bad News Bears roles before mid-teens. Family domain advantages are not documented. He later pivoted to engineering via Stanford and founded Lutter Consulting at 24, later serving as CTO at firms including Cumulus Media, E*Offering, and Lynda.com—notable but specialist-level software career relative to childhood screen fame.
starting_point: Born 1962 in Ridgewood, New Jersey; childhood spent there before early film career; family industry background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Entrepreneur and engineer; founder of Lutter Consulting; former CTO roles including Cumulus Media, E*Offering, and Lynda.com; lives in the U.S. (Park City area reported in recent profiles).

trajectory.event: Starred as Tommy in Scorsese’s Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore; later BAFTA-nominated as Most Promising Newcomer.
Played brainy Alfred Ogilvie in The Bad News Bears and its 1977 sequel, capping a busy child-acting run.
Earned a BS in civil engineering from Stanford University.
Founded Lutter Consulting, providing technology strategy and outsourced software development.
Completed an MS in management and engineering at Stanford.
Continued executive technology roles, later including CTO positions at Cumulus Media, E*Offering, and Lynda.com.

name: Marco Falke
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; Bitcoin Core maintainer from ~2016 with 2000+ commits, but age at start of contributions cannot be verified as ≤26.
early_history_summary: Marco Falke became a prolific Bitcoin Core contributor and QA/testing maintainer from about 2016, accumulating over 2,000 commits before stepping down from the maintainer role in 2023; funded at times by Okcoin and Paradigm.
evidence_summary: Public coverage focuses on 2016–2023 maintainer tenure. Without a documented birth year, eligibility by age 26 cannot be established. Wikipedia page linked in the candidate CSV is not a usable personal biography.

name: Joe Armstrong
milestone_by_age_26: Erlang co-invented at Ericsson in 1986 at age ~35–36; earlier UCL physics B.Sc. (1972) and brief AI work under Donald Michie are not material field-defining milestones by 26.
early_history_summary: Born 1950 in Bournemouth; programmed Fortran on a council mainframe at 17; B.Sc. Physics UCL 1972; brief AI research with Donald Michie at Edinburgh; moved to Sweden 1974; Ericsson CS Lab from 1984 where he co-designed Erlang with Virding and Williams.
evidence_summary: Serious programming started young, but the career-defining language design and open-source release (1998) came in middle age. No dated material public milestone by age 26 beyond ordinary early career steps.

name: Peter Todd
milestone_by_age_26: Early cypherpunk emails as a teen and Bitcointalk posts ~2010 are not material field milestones; first Bitcoin Core code contributions reported ~April 2012 (about age 27 if born ~1985). CSV birth year 1980 is not corroborated by major bios.
early_history_summary: Canadian developer; reported communication with cypherpunks (Adam Back, Hal Finney) from about age 15; art school (OCAD); early Bitcoin forum activity ~2010; Core contributor from ~2012; later OpenTimestamps and protocol security work; 2024 HBO film falsely alleged he is Satoshi (he denied).
evidence_summary: Press around the HBO documentary places him near age 39 in 2024 (~1985 birth) and describes 2010 forum activity at about 25 without a standalone breakthrough. Material Core development impact is associated with the 2010s after age 26. Birth year is not fixed on Wikipedia.

name: H. D. Moore
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Metasploit Project in summer 2003 at about age 22, creating an open-source penetration-testing framework that became the industry-standard exploit development and testing platform.
early_history_summary: Born 1981 (Honolulu per secondary profiles); dropped out of high school for about two years before returning; first professional security role at age 17 developing tools for the U.S. Department of Defense; continued exploit and audit work, then launched Metasploit as a public exploit research resource in 2003 while still in his early 20s.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources; some secondary profiles describe a difficult childhood and early independence, but primary family financial/domain facts are sparse.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Metasploit, DoD teen work, exploit research, open source security, full disclosure, Rapid7, runZero
evidence_summary: Moore’s path is self-driven technical depth: DoD security tooling at 17 after dropping out of high school, then founding Metasploit at ~22, which defined modern penetration testing. Family capital and elite-school pipelines are not documented; advantages center on early scarce skills, online security communities, and intense hands-on exploit practice. Later roles include Rapid7 CRO after Metasploit’s 2009 acquisition and co-founding runZero (formerly Rumble).
starting_point: Born 1981; childhood reportedly included moves (Honolulu origin in secondary profiles); left high school for two years before returning and entering security work young; family finances not well documented.
current_position: Co-founder and CTO of runZero (cyber asset attack surface management); former Rapid7 chief research officer and Metasploit chief architect.

trajectory.event: Took a DoD-linked security research/development role writing exploits and traffic-capture tooling while still a teenager.
Founded the Metasploit Project as a public exploit research and penetration-testing framework.
Ran the Month of Browser Bugs full-disclosure campaign, driving browser patches and industry attention.
Metasploit was acquired by Rapid7; Moore became a senior security executive while remaining Metasploit architect.
Left Rapid7 after years as chief research officer / Metasploit chief architect.
Co-founded Rumble (later runZero) for network discovery and attack-surface management.
Company rebranded to runZero; continued as co-founder and CTO.

name: Shekhar Bhansali
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; academic career milestones (RMIT lecturer 1995, USF faculty 2000, NSF CAREER 2003) cannot be age-verified as ≤26.
early_history_summary: Indian-trained engineer (NIT Jaipur, IIT Madras, PhD RMIT) who built a U.S. academic career in MEMS/biosensors, led ECE at FIU, directed NSF ECCS, and later chaired ECE at Vanderbilt; IEEE Fellow 2023.
evidence_summary: Without birth year, age at PhD, first faculty roles, or CAREER award cannot be confirmed at or before 26. Public record emphasizes mid-career research leadership rather than a documented early breakthrough.

name: Mike Cafarella
category: Computer scientist / Hadoop and Nutch co-founder
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year (Wikipedia: year of birth missing); Nutch/Hadoop work ~2002–2006 and PhD 2009 cannot be verified as occurring at age ≤26.
early_history_summary: Brown BS 1996, Edinburgh MSc AI 1997, UW PhD 2009; co-founded Nutch with Doug Cutting and contributed to Hadoop origins; later Michigan faculty, Lattice Data (Apple acquisition), MIT CSAIL principal research scientist.
evidence_summary: If one assumes typical ages for a 1996 bachelor’s degree, Nutch/Hadoop activity would likely fall after age 26, but eligibility requires a confirmed birth year and dated ≤26 milestone. Neither is established in reviewed sources.

name: Krishna Bharat
milestone_by_age_26: Google News (~2001–02, age ~31–32) and Hilltop work at DEC SRC were after 26; IIT Madras B.Tech (1991) and Georgia Tech PhD (1996, age 26) are educational credentials, not treated here as standalone material public milestones.
early_history_summary: Born 1970 in Bengaluru; St. Joseph’s Boys’ High School; IIT Madras CS B.Tech 1991; Georgia Tech PhD HCI 1996; DEC SRC (Hilltop with Mihaila); joined Google 1999; created Google News after 9/11; later opened Google India R&D and returned as distinguished research scientist.
evidence_summary: Conservative call: PhD completion at 26 is noteworthy but not a field-defining public breakthrough comparable to Google News. Defining product and algorithm milestones landed in his late 20s and 30s.

name: Marc Tarpenning
milestone_by_age_26: NuvoMedia/Rocket eBook (1997–98, age ~33–34) and Tesla co-founding (2003, age 39) both after 26; UC Berkeley CS BA (1985) and early engineering jobs are not material breakout milestones by 26.
early_history_summary: Born June 1, 1964 in Sacramento; Berkeley CS 1985; Textron in Saudi Arabia then software/firmware roles (Seagate, Bechtel, Packet Design); co-founded NuvoMedia (sold to Gemstar for ~$187M in 2000); co-founded Tesla with Martin Eberhard in 2003 as CFO/VP engineering until 2008.
evidence_summary: Early career shows solid engineering employment and elite education, but the first independently material entrepreneurial milestone (NuvoMedia) came in his 30s. Tesla success was later still.
